Context

§league constants

Baseball Feature Atlas

Every input to the moneyline models, one card each: what the builder actually computes, how often it is a stand-in value rather than a measurement, and how each model responds to it across its range.

Two models sit side by side. 3L is the production 3-league model (KBO + LMB + MLB, 14 inputs) — the one that prices the daily card. 2L is the experimental fork that drops LMB and adds the two park columns, 17 inputs. Every production input is also in the fork, so most cards carry both; the three the fork alone uses — the two park columns and EMA_RD_Diff, retired from production on 17 Aug 2026 — are marked 2-league only. The three split team-offense Elos that joined both models on 4 Sep 2026 are marked added 4 Sep.

Because the fork changes two things at once — the league pool and the park features — a gap between the curves is not a clean read on either. The head-to-head table below splits them by league, which is as close to like-for-like as these two get.

Production 3-league vs the 2-league park fork

Whole-card ROI is not a fair comparison — the two models bet different games. This splits each league out of each model, so KBO is judged against KBO and MLB against MLB. Bets at edge > 5%, model head only, no GNN blend, one seed-42 run — the model-card ROIs above average five seeds, so they differ by a few tenths. The counts are small enough that a handful of results swings these by percentage points: read the direction, not the decimal.

MLB+8.9% n=427+8.9% n=395+5.1% n=481+8.7% n=451

all bets+3.1% n=799+5.9% n=554+7.1% n=831+10.5% n=593

SHAP share — mean |SHAP| in log-odds as a fraction of all of that model's inputs (14 / 17), for the 3-league and 2-league model. Says how much a model uses a feature, not whether using it helps.

Defaulted — the share of games where the builder substituted a neutral stand-in (no history for that pitcher, team or park) instead of a measurement. Every column here is populated on every row, so this is the honest coverage number.

dBrier if dropped — the model's own walk-forward re-run without that one column, paired: each seed is run with and without the feature and the differences averaged, so the shared randomness cancels instead of swamping the effect. Positive = removing it made the model worse, so it was earning its place; negative = the model was better without it. Greyed out means the paired mean is inside two standard errors of itself. The n/5 beside the label counts how many seeds agreed on the sign — a verdict resting on 3/5 is weaker than the mean alone suggests.

What this does not control is the era. All five seeds share one dataset and one 2024-26 validation window, so a resolved verdict here means "reliable given this data", not "reliable in general".

PDP / ICE — sweep the feature across its range on 400 held-out games. The threads are individual games, the line their average in the 3-league model, the dashed line the 2-league model's. Threads that cross or fan out mean the feature only acts through interactions.

Diagnostics are measured on the 2024-2026 validation era with the model trained on everything before 2024 — the first fold of its own walk-forward, so none of this is in-sample. The production GNN blend (0.7 model / 0.3 GNN) is not applied: it damps every feature effect uniformly and would only blur the attribution.

Formula build_timeseries_with_lineup.py:408 (get_team_woba_blended)
wOBA_Diff = Home_wOBA_Blended - Away_wOBA_Blended        # NaN -> 100

per team, from every batter who has appeared for it so far this season:
    OBP    = (H + BB + HBP) / (AB + BB + HBP)
    ISO    = HR / AB                       # HR only - 2B and 3B contribute nothing
    wOBA   = 0.7*OBP + 0.9*ISO + 0.320
    wOBA+  = wOBA / 0.320 * 100
    ytd    = sum(wOBA+ * AB) / sum(AB)     # AB-weighted across the roster
    decay  = min(1, team_games / 25)
    Home_wOBA_Blended = decay*ytd + (1 - decay)*preseason_projection

Not Fangraphs wOBA — a hand-rolled index, and ISO is HR/AB rather than SLG-AVG, so a doubles-driven offence is invisible to it. The +0.320 sits inside the ratio, which lifts the whole index: an average team scores ~180, not 100. That makes the fillna(100) fallback in add_derived_features a trap — a team with no batter rows would enter the model ~80 points below the worst real offence rather than as neutral. It never fires in the backtest (zero nulls) but it is live-scoring risk.

12.4% / 12.4% SHAP share 3L / 2L
0.549univariate AUC
5.9%defaulted
+0.00012 / +0.00002 dBrier if dropped 3L 5/5 · 2L 3/5
Formula build_timeseries_with_lineup.py:671 + 3league_final.py:124 (_shrink)
Starter_K_BB_Diff = shrink(home_blend) - shrink(away_blend)

blend, per starter:
    K/BB   = SO / BB
    K_BB+  = K/BB / lg_KBB * 100
             150 if BB == 0 and SO > 0     # hard-coded escape hatch
             100 if BB == 0 and SO == 0
    decay  = min(1, starts / 6)
    blend  = decay*K_BB+ + (1 - decay)*preseason_projection

shrink(x, sd, ref_sd):                  # 3league_final.py:124, _shrink()
    confidence = 1 / (1 + sd / ref_sd)     # sd == ref_sd -> exactly 50% shrink
    return 100 + (x - 100) * confidence

ref_sd comes from a 3x2 table per league, picked by the pitcher's Glicko:
    <=1525 'weak' | <=1625 'avg' | >1625 'strong'
    KBO whip .802/.738/.595   kbb .488/.480/.413
    LMB whip .850/.850/.700   kbb .500/.500/.450
    MLB whip .780/.720/.580   kbb .480/.470/.420

The name says K-BB% but the formula is the K/BB ratio, and a ratio with a small denominator explodes: median 100, but the blended value reaches 1240 and the SD is 57 — six times the WHIP feature's. Those extremes are a walk-count artefact (two walks in a start), not talent, and the model sees them as the largest pitching edges in the dataset. Same 23% flat-shrink gap as the WHIP twin.

Off_Hand_Diff = Home_MOV_Off_vsHand_Elo - Away_MOV_Off_vsHand_Elo

each lineup keeps two extra offense Elos, one per opposing starter hand:
    home key = (home team, hand of the AWAY starter)    # from Away_Starter_L, unknown = R
    away key = (away team, hand of the HOME starter)
the two keyed ratings play each other, same margin outcome as the team rating:
    s        = 1 / (1 + exp(-(home_runs - away_runs) / 3.0))
    expected = 1 / (1 + 10^((away_key - home_key) / 400))
    home_key += 24 * (s - expected);  away_key -= the same amount
season boundary: rating -> 1500 + 0.5*(rating - 1500)
no game yet in that split: 1500

ADDED TO PRODUCTION 4 Sep 2026, with the two venue boosts below. All three together moved the walk-forward Brier edge on bettable games from +0.0005 to +0.0010 and ROI from +7.3% to +9.0%, with the gain in MLB and KBO/LMB flat. This one is not a platoon split in the usual sense: it rates the whole lineup against left- or right-handed STARTERS, updated on the run margin of the game, so it carries everything else the overall rating carries. That shows in the correlation panel at 0.87 with MOV_Team_Off_Elo_Diff, and in a spread almost as wide (SD 47 against 50). The vs-LHP side only updates in about 27% of games, so a team's left-handed rating moves on a third of the evidence of its right-handed one. A missed handedness lookup routes the game to the R side.

Formula build_timeseries_with_lineup.py:651 + 3league_final.py:124 (_shrink)
Starter_WHIP_Diff = shrink(home_blend) - shrink(away_blend)

blend, per starter:
    WHIP   = (H + BB) / IP
    WHIP+  = lg_WHIP / WHIP * 100          # inverted: above 100 = better
    decay  = min(1, starts / 6)
    blend  = decay*WHIP+ + (1 - decay)*preseason_projection

shrink(x, sd, ref_sd):                  # 3league_final.py:124, _shrink()
    confidence = 1 / (1 + sd / ref_sd)     # sd == ref_sd -> exactly 50% shrink
    return 100 + (x - 100) * confidence

ref_sd comes from a 3x2 table per league, picked by the pitcher's Glicko:
    <=1525 'weak' | <=1625 'avg' | >1625 'strong'
    KBO whip .802/.738/.595   kbb .488/.480/.413
    LMB whip .850/.850/.700   kbb .500/.500/.450
    MLB whip .780/.720/.580   kbb .480/.470/.420

The shrink weight is the pitcher's own recent volatility: SD of his last 10 starts' WHIP, needing 3 starts to exist. It is missing on 23% of rows, and the fallback sets sd = ref_sd, i.e. a flat 50% shrink toward 100 — so roughly a quarter of games run this feature at half strength. The SD itself is fragile at the tail (max 37 on a 0.63 median, from short outings), and a large SD drives confidence to ~0, pinning the pitcher at exactly league average.

Formula 3league_final.py:369 (compute_mov_glicko2) / :317 (_glicko2_update)
MOV_Starter_Elo_Diff = Home_MOV_Starter_Elo - Away_MOV_Starter_Elo
                       (pre-game ratings; the column name says Elo, the values are Glicko-2)

per game, chronologically over all leagues at once:
    s = 1 / (1 + exp(-(home_runs - away_runs) / 3.0))    # margin, not W/L
    each starter gets a one-game Glicko-2 update against the other's rating,
    keyed '<LEAGUE>_<pitcher name>' so the pools never mix

season boundary:
    rating -> 1500 + 0.5*(rating - 1500)
    RD     -> min(350, sqrt(RD^2 + 100^2))              # off-season uncertainty
unseen pitcher: 1500, RD 350, vol 0.06

The one rating in the set that is uncertainty-aware, which is why it beat plain Elo for pitchers: a rookie's RD is wide so his first starts move him fast. Because the outcome is sigmoid(run diff / 3), it is a run-margin rating rather than a win rating — a 1-0 shutout scores 0.58, a 7-run win 0.91. It is also the model's own bet filter: a game is only bettable if the side being backed has the higher rating, so this feature gates the card as well as feeding it.

0.0%defaulted

Formula build_timeseries_with_lineup.py:1305 + :1413 (K_BB_vs_Opp)
K_BB_Mismatch_Diff = Home_K_BB_vs_Opp - Away_K_BB_vs_Opp        # NaN -> 0

Home_K_BB_vs_Opp = home_starter_K_BB_blend - away_team_K_rate_index
Away_K_BB_vs_Opp = away_starter_K_BB_blend - home_team_K_rate_index

where the team index is
    k_rate = sum(SO) / sum(AB)  over the roster to date
    index  = k_rate / 0.20 * 100           # 0.22 in MLB

Two things to check here. First the units: a SO/BB ratio index is being subtracted from a SO/AB rate index — they share a 100 label and nothing else. Second the sign: a lineup that strikes out often scores a HIGH k-rate index, and the formula subtracts it, so facing a whiff-prone offence makes the mismatch term smaller, not larger. Read literally that is backwards from the feature's name. It also inherits the K/BB tail (SD 58, max 1131), so its extremes are the same walk-count artefacts.

RETIRED FROM PRODUCTION on 17 Aug 2026; still an input to the 2-league fork. Paired leave-one-out — the same seed run with and without it — improved the production model's Brier in 5 of 5 seeds, mean -0.00022 against a standard error of 0.00003. The reason is visible in the correlation panel: it sits at 0.74 with MOV_Team_Off_Elo_Diff, which carries the same run-differential signal opponent-adjusted and margin-mapped, while this one is raw. It is the only outcome-based input rather than a rate, so it takes blowouts at full weight — a single 12-run game moves it more than a fortnight of one-run wins — and seeding on the first game leaves it twice as loud before a team has 10 games (mean |value| 3.56 against 1.71 after). In August the same test did not resolve on the 2-league fork, whose validation set is 24% smaller, so it stayed there. Re-run on the 14 Oct 2026 data, with the split offense Elos in both models, it now resolves on the fork too: Brier better without it in 5 of 5 seeds, mean -0.00018 against a standard error of 0.00007. The ROI effect was ~0 in production: a calibration cleanup, not a betting change.

Added 4 Sep 2026 (see Off_Hand_Diff). Read it as how much better a team plays at home than its overall rating says. The overall rating already includes the same home games, so the boost is a difference between two ratings that share half their evidence. It is narrow as a result: SD 19, against 50 for the overall difference. Its correlation with MOV_Team_Off_Elo_Diff is -0.31, the expected sign, since a strong team's home-only rating lags its overall one early in a season. A team before its first home game enters at 1500 minus its overall rating, which is the stand-in counted in the coverage panel.

    decay  = min(1, team_games / 25)

Team-level and undated — it is the whole season's relief work to date, so it says nothing about who is actually available tonight (no rest, no usage, no leverage). Bullpen_Fatigue and Bullpen_Depth exist in the timeseries and are not in FEATURE_COLS. The index averages 88 rather than 100 because relief innings run worse than the flat league WHIP constant it is divided by.

Formula 3league_final.py:459 (venue keys) / :513 (Off_Away_Boost)
Off_Away_Boost = Away_MOV_Off_Away_Elo - Away_MOV_Team_Off_Elo

per team, an offense Elo updated only in its ROAD games:
    key (team, 'A') plays the host's (team, 'H') rating
    same margin outcome s, K = 24, season regression 0.5 toward 1500
the boost is that road-only rating minus the team's overall offense Elo

The mirror of Off_Home_Boost, taken from the visiting team's side, so it is not a home-minus-away difference like the rest of the set. The model sees home's home edge and away's road edge as two separate columns, and the two are almost uncorrelated (0.03). Same width (SD 19), same half-shared evidence with the overall rating, and same stand-in before a team's first road game.

Formula 2league_park_experimental.py:224
Park_Factor_Sq = (Park_Factor - 1.0) ** 2      # distance from neutral, squared

A curvature term borrowed from linear-model habits, again 2-league only. A tree does not need it: any monotone transform of a feature it already has gives the same achievable splits, so this can only re-order ties among the same 38 discrete values. It is also sign-blind — Coors and Petco are far from neutral in opposite directions and this column cannot tell them apart. Watch whether its SHAP share is coming out of Park_Factor rather than adding to it.

Formula 2league_park_experimental.py:94 (load_run_park_factors) / :112 (_park_key)
Park_Factor = 0.7 * PF_Avg + 0.3 * PF_HR       # PF_HR_WEIGHT = 0.30
              keyed on the HOME team, unmapped -> 1.0

KBO / MLB   OOTP27 researched park data, joined teams.csv -> parks.csv
            (ootp27_database/build_park_factors.py, build_mlb_park_factors.py)
LMB         empirical Cramer factors from the boxscores, pooled 2016-2025:
                PF_HR  = (HR/game at home)  / (HR/game on the road)
                PF_Avg = (H/AB at home)     / (H/AB on the road)
                shrunk 1 + n/(n+200) * (raw - 1),  n = min(home, road games)

name fixes before lookup: KBO short -> full via KBO_TEAM_MAP, then
St. Louis spacing, Cleveland Indians -> Guardians, Oakland Athletics -> Athletics

Only the 2-league fork uses this; the production model has no park input at all, so the panels here are KBO + MLB (the LMB builder exists and feeds the 3-league park fork, which is not the model shown). Static per team and never varying by date, it is also a coarse team identity: 8 distinct values across the 10 KBO clubs (Doosan and LG share Jamsil, Kiwoom and Samsung coincide) and 30 in MLB. Any signal it carries beyond the physical park is team identity leaking in under another name. Two known staleness points: OOTP lists NC Dinos at Masan although they moved to Changwon in 2019, and PF_Avg is a batting-average factor, so Jamsil reads 0.99 on contact and 0.61 on home runs — the 0.7/0.3 composite is what keeps that park from looking neutral. Nothing defaults to 1.0 in the baseline, so the alias table is currently complete.

Formula 3league_final.py:63 (FEATURE_COLS) / 2league_park_experimental.py:52
League = 0 KBO, 1 LMB, 2 MLB        # 3-league model
         0 KBO, 1 MLB               # 2-league model — same column, different meaning

XGBoost treats this as a number, not a category, so in the 3-league model a split at League < 1.5 groups KBO with LMB against MLB, and there is no single split that isolates LMB. The ordering happens to be defensible (the two smaller leagues share a run environment) but it is an accident of the coding, not a decision. Its real job is to soak up the per-league offsets in the constants table above — which is why adding the park features pushed it down the importance list: the park term explains part of the same run-environment gap.

Formula 3league_final.py:143 (_get_hand), models/pitcher_handedness.csv
Home_Starter_L = 1 if hand == 'L' else 0

lookup order:
    1. (starter name, league) in pitcher_handedness.csv
    2. starter name alone, any league
    3. 'R'                                  # not found
missing starter name -> 0

A miss and a right-hander produce the same 0, so the feature cannot say 'unknown'. The cache holds 2,690 pitchers (1,223 MLB / 958 LMB / 509 KBO), 26% of them left-handed; the coverage panel opposite shows how often the starter on the card is not in it. There is no batter-side platoon split anywhere in FEATURE_COLS, so handedness has nothing to interact with — the model can only learn 'lefties are worth x runs', not the matchup.

The constants each league is indexed against

Every rate feature above is an index — a stat divided by a league average, times 100. Those denominators are hard-coded per builder and never re-centred downstream, so the same column means slightly different things in different rows of the same training set. This is the offset the League indicator spends its capacity on.
